thread:
incidents-bot: ALERT · SSO anomaly detected for service-account@redwood-corp.com — 128 sign-in attempts from 3 regions in 180s. Possible automated push/replay. Alert: sso-1729954321

maria_g: saw this. logs show many ACCEPT events but also a spike in challenge_push_sent for the same account.

samir: can you paste a small log sample? curious about user-agent and X-Forwarded-For.

maria_g: digging. snippet:```
2024-11-03T14:12:01Z accept user=service-account src=10.3.2.14 ua="curl/7.85" region=us-east-1 challenge=push_sent
2024-11-03T14:12:04Z accept user=service-account src=52.9.1.211 ua="node-fetch/1.0" region=eu-west-1 challenge=push_sent
2024-11-03T14:12:11Z accept user=service-account src=3.120.44.9 ua="python-requests/2.28" region=ap-southeast-1 challenge=push_sent
```

lee_ops: pattern looks like distributed replay. IPs are cloud provider ranges, likely botnet or misconfigured automation. any abnormal session revokes?

jordan_p: yes — we have a wave of session_revoked events for human users when these push requests hit. Could be MFA fatigue due to mass push storms.

irene_sec: immediate actions: 1) throttle challenge_push for service-account on auth-edge (rate limit to 5/min) 2) revoke any active sessions created in the last 10m for that account 3) add src IP ranges to temporary denylist in WAF. agrees? @lee_ops @samir

samir: agree. throttling rule deployed to auth-edge:```yaml
- match: request.user == "service-account"
  action: rate_limit
  limit: 5/min
```
Implementing denylist for the 3 suspect ranges now.

lee_ops: ran `POST /internal/sessions/revoke` for user=service-account token_age<=600s, got 202. pushing a follow-up job to ensure caches cleared.

maria_g: contact log from KMS shows no rotation events. keys look fine. but question: should we rotate the principal's API key or rotate KMS key? rotating API creds first seems sufficient.

irene_sec: rotate creds for that service-account and require new key material via KMS unwrap for any automation. Also add MFA backstop for interactive logins only. we should avoid rotating KMS root key unless we see compromise of key material.

jordan_p: communications: ops oncall to notify affected product teams, security will open an incident page. short message for status page?

maria_g: draft status: "We've observed an automated sign-in storm targeting a service account. We have throttled authentication attempts and revoked recent sessions. No customer data exposure detected. Investigation ongoing." thoughts?

irene_sec: clean. add mitigation steps and ETA for full root cause in 2 hours. set severity to sev2 for now.

oncall-bot: oncall pager assigned to @lee_ops for 1h.

samir: I pulled audit logs for the last 24h for that principal and flagged any unusual grant events. only standard svc role was used. attaching csv to incident doc.

lee_ops: created short-term alert rule to detect >10 push_sent events for a single principal in 60s and escalate to eng-security.

maria_g: post-incident followups: 1) add per-principal challenge_push rate limits 2) require client assertion signing for service-account rotation (JWT with kid pinned) 3) enhance audit logging to include device_fingerprint header 

irene_sec: add RBAC review: ensure service-account has least privilege and rotate keys on schedule. also file vuln triage to see if any auth edge bug allowed push abuse.

jordan_p: ask product teams if any automation used that account — @product-leads? (ping from channel)

maria_g: we've paused that account's API tokens and issued a new pair. automation owners will update during maintenance window.

lee_ops: running a quick scan for similar patterns across other tenants, will post findings in 30m. preliminary: 5 other principals saw small spikes, all contained by edge throttles.

irene_sec: good. creating followup ticket: SEC-2024-401 · "MFA push amplification mitigation" with action items: throttles, audit enrich, cred rotation, RBAC review, runbook update. assigning owners.

samir: one question — do we want a KMS integration change to sign auth assertions (so pushes require KMS-signed tokens)? pros/cons?

maria_g: pro: harder to replay without key material. con: latency and complexity for service-to-service calls. propose optional enforcement for high-risk principals.

irene_sec: capture that in ticket. also schedule tabletop next week to rehearse push-flood scenario.

jordan_p: will prepare the incident summary and timeline once lee_ops posts the scan.

lee_ops: scan results: attached small list, all were blocked or throttled, no creds reused. updating incident doc.

maria_g: final note: we should add an operator-facing metric for "challenge_push_rate_per_principal" in console so product teams can see noisy principals before it escalates.

irene_sec: agreed. closing immediate mitigation. will update once RCA is ready. :white_check_mark:
